reviews.text:
As the days are hot these days, I'm thinking about eating eel rice bowls and want to stop by Yunagi, which I visited last year. I happened to come across this place, Dumpling Man, and decided to eat some dumplings as an appetizer before heading out.

The store was located in an alley behind Soonchunhyang Hospital near the Hannam branch of Pumpkin Restaurant, which I recently stopped by. When I entered the store, which seemed to be a semi-basement that was probably a remodeled old parking lot, the seats consisted of only counter seats, which were deep inside in a U-shape, and there was a kitchen further inside.

When I told him I was alone, he told me to sit down because it was comfortable, so I sat in the seat near the entrance and tried the meat dumplings. If I liked it, I decided to try another menu item that I was curious about, the curry fried dumplings. I also asked for a meat dumpling, which felt like a basic menu item.

After giving me a plastic bottle filled with water, I looked at the counter and saw that there was an hourglass, slightly spicy pickled radish, and yuzu soy sauce instead of the usual soy sauce.

After drinking water and waiting for a while, he finally set up a steamer with meat dumplings in front of me, flipped the hourglass over, and said that if you eat it after resting for 3 minutes, the dumpling skin will be more chewy and that the dumplings do not contain any seasoning and are only seasoned with shiitake mushrooms or other ingredients, and that you can eat them by dipping them in yuzu soy sauce.

Looking at the dumplings, I thought they would be fine as long as they tasted good and had a decent amount of volume. I waited for the sand in the hourglass to fall to the bottom.

Finally, after 3 minutes, I lifted the dumpling skin carefully without tearing it and dipped it in the yuzu sauce and took a bite, excited to see what it would taste like. I felt like I was eating pumpkin dumplings that my mom used to make for me when I was young. I could feel each and every vegetable in it. Whether it is good to feel that way is a matter of likes or dislikes, but crucially, I sometimes felt a bitter taste and the texture felt somewhat like paste, so I thought, what is this?

I know that they worked hard to make these dumplings so that you can feel all the good ingredients, but those ingredients should come together to give the feel of meat dumplings, but it just ends in the feeling of various ingredients, and I can't come up with the right word in Korean, such as paste, but in English, I don't like the mushy texture, so I said, "Hmm, I don't have to taste other dumplings anymore."

As I was eating, the filling of the dumpling fell on the plate in front of me and I tried to pick it up with my chopsticks, but the unpleasant mushy texture that I felt in my mouth was also visible on the plate in front of me, so I guess it was like that.

I'm sorry, but I didn't order any more, got up, paid, and came out.

Overall, I discovered this dumpling restaurant by chance, so I was wondering if I could taste delicious dumplings. It was introduced on Mango Girl Street, so I hurriedly stopped by and tried the meat dumplings to see if there would be a lot of customers. It felt like they were trying to offer some unique dumplings, but the taste and texture were disappointing, so I didn't like it.

Hannam [Sweat Sweat]⠀
Galleria ‘Gourmet 494’ opened in ‘Nine One’, a newly built luxury villa in Hannam-dong. It is the first urban platform introduced by Gourmet 494, which existed only as the Apgujeong Luxury Hall of Galleria Department Store and the Daejeon Time World Food Hall. ‘Gourmet 494’ is a premium food hall that Galleria opened at the Apgujeong-dong Luxury Hall in 2012, and is the first food boutique in Korea to offer select dining and Grocery+Restaurant at the same time. ‘Gourmet 494 Hannam’ can be seen as a premium lifestyle platform with the concept of ‘Fine Living’, which combines the fine dining of the existing ‘Gourmet 494’ with high-quality lifestyle content such as a popular F&B brand and fine dining restaurant, a premium lifestyle brand suited to the regional characteristics and high-end residential environment of Hannam-dong, and ‘Maison Galleria’, a VIP facility.
⠀
Recently, trendy businesses are all gathered in one place. There were a variety of other businesses, including [Blue Bottle], an American specialty coffee shop, [Our Bakery] operated by CNP Foods, Cheongdam's famous brunch café [Anderson's], Korean beef omakase restaurant [Surin], French-style Chinese restaurant [Piese], sushi omakase restaurant [Sushinoyaya], and Kaisendon restaurant [Oboksusan]. Branding through space is also an important element for restaurants these days, so there are many cases where they lose their identity when they open in a department store, but Gourmet 494 Hannam seems to have made a good compromise on such issues by developing its own space in a sophisticated manner.⠀
Although I had a hard time deciding between the various options, I had lunch at [Tamttam] that day. [Tam Tam] is a restaurant well known for its ‘offal rice noodles’ menu and was originally located near Gangnam Station. Personally, I don’t like tripe that much (don’t stop following me…) so I ordered ‘Spicy Beef Pork Rice Noodles’ and ‘Charcoal-grilled Pork Rice Noodles’. The spiciness is level 2, and is said to be about as spicy as hot chicken stir-fry noodles. Not only did I feel the spicy taste of the peppers, but I also felt a tingling taste from the marinara. The seasoning was just right so it tasted delicious even though it was spicy, and the fatty taste from the generous amount of beef pork was also good. ‘Charcoal-grilled pork rice bowl’ can be thought of as a menu item that replaces the noodles with rice. The ribs, which were moderately seasoned, were more tender than expected. It just feels like eating delicious pork ribs. It was a menu that seemed to have no likes or dislikes. Overall, the menu items were well seasoned and of high quality.
⠀
‘Gourmet Hannam 494’ feels like an appropriate blend of trendiness and the luxurious feel of the existing Apgujeong luxury store, Gourmet 494. Wouldn’t it become a new landmark of Hannam-dong? It will survive.

The softly flowing jazz music completes the mood of the space, and the kindness of the servers and detailed explanations of the menu increase expectations/satisfaction.

Mill Gnocchi: The flavor of aged cheese (Parmigiano Reggiano), fried olive bread crumbs, and bacon harmonize.
However, the gnocchi was too soft and the chewiness of the gnocchi was somewhat disappointing.

Mill Lasagna: Deep meaty ragu sauce and tomato flavor spread throughout your mouth. The texture is very soft, making it easy to enjoy without stress.

Millhouse Tteokbokki: Seafood Tteokbokki served at just the right time when you start feeling greasy. Soft rice cakes, fish cakes, and mussels combine to create a spicy sauce with a kick. A clear sauce, not a thick sauce.
Luxurious spicy taste.

Dessert: Creme brûlée is a combination of crispy sugar coating and fluffy custard cream inside, and rice risotto/basil risotto fills your mouth with each flavor.

A place you'll definitely want to visit again as it has an excellent balance of atmosphere, service, and taste.

reviews.author: ANNEZUE
reviews.text:
I had lunch. It was interesting to see pumpkins of odd shapes all over the place. They didn't give me a glass of water until my group arrived, so I called the older female server in front of me to ask for water, and she said, "Oh, yes," and poured me some water. I noticed that she wasn't very friendly. Haha. When my group arrived, I decided to order a main course, but he was in front of me. Then, he called a younger male server and had him do the work for me. He seemed to work according to my taste. It didn't look good. There were no wet tissues on the table, so I asked for them and only then did they give me some. There was a female server in front of me, so I asked for the drink list. She said, “We have cola and cider.” I asked to see the list because I wanted to order wine, but she quietly brought the drink list as if she was really bothered. It looks like the older female server needs service training~
First, a welcome snack came out. The chef's hometown is Taean, so it was made with seasonal seafood and ingredients brought from Taean, and it was topped with dried snow crab meat and topped with mugwort and mugwort. He said it was good to whet the appetite, and the crispy seaweed flakes and crab meat, similar to sashimi and green, were good. I didn't even eat the food, but as soon as the explanation was over, the next food came out, so I was impatient. It was a dish made with a Western-style pumpkin called butternut squash. This pumpkin looks like a peanut, so it is also called a peanut pumpkin. It was fascinating to see it in real life. The soup was topped with white shrimp from Taean. It was a very smooth pumpkin porridge with plump shrimp meat on top.
The third dish was carpaccio using wild flounder. It was served with herbs and oil, but the flounder was cut into bite-size pieces, and the salt from Taean called Songhwayeom on the side was said to be a slightly sweet salt made from pine resin powder and sea salt, but it didn't go well with carpaccio and wasn't sweet. It was just salty. Herbs, celery, and cherry tomatoes were on top of the food. The flounder was chewy and tasted just like a salad. The salt didn't go well with the food at all.
The fourth dish was octopus cooked on charcoal, garnished with Sumi potatoes from Taean, paprika, and carrots. I cut it with an octopus knife, but it was too tough. The rich flavor of the potatoes was very strong. It felt like steamed octopus. It was just not good.
The fifth dish was oil pasta. The noodles were thin spaghetti noodles with zucchini, Taean seaweed, clams, mussels, and clams, and on top were daisy daisy and young shoots. It was just oil pasta with salty seaweed. I was surprised at first because the pickled olives that came with it smelled like poop, but I got used to it as I ate it, so I ate it two more times.
Sixth came the grilled bottle fish. It was baked in the oven for a long time to add softness, and the green sauce was said to be an Italian-style sauce using green onions. Next to it, they prepared green onions to boil off the sweetness, but the green onions were blackened. It was the best of all the food that came out. It was very soft bottlenose meat, but the outside was soft and dry and savory. The green sauce was like eating raw green onions with just the outer layer, and the sauce was difficult.
The seventh main dish came out. We ordered beef, pork, and sheep, and the sauce was black garlic paste, a sauce made by steeping calf bones, and the eggplant on the right was prepared by spreading basil pesto grown on the farm in Taean and lightly roasting it in the oven. It had arugula, chaatni made with paprika below, and pine flower salt. Lamb was the most tender, followed by pork, and finally beef. The beef was tender and everything was delicious.
The eighth dish was ice cream sherbet using pears, and various nuts were used below to add flavor. Next to it was a pear cut that was easy to eat, which was nice. It was a home-baked madeleine and a fig tart. It was a moist tart-like cookie with figs and not-so-sweet cream, so I ate it gently. The madeleine was a little tough and chewy.
I was full, but the food wasn't tasty.
I don't think I will visit again

reviews.text:
Personally, I think this restaurant is the best soup restaurant in Seoul.
As the weather got chilly, I wanted to try French onion soup, so I visited the restaurant specializing in soups and stews. After hearing what the owner said, I realized that there aren't many soup restaurants in Korea.
He said he missed the soup he used to eat in the U.S. and made it himself.
As you can tell from the name, clam chowder soup is the most popular menu item, and French onion soup is said to be served during the cold season. In the case of French Onion, it would take some time, so I contacted them first and visited, as they said I would need to contact them about 20 minutes in advance.
I ordered French onion and chili soup, and both were the best soups I've ever had in terms of rich ingredients and flavor.
The French Onion had a sweet flavor from the onions that had been boiled for a long time and the rich flavor of the cheese, making it perfect for eating in the winter, while the Chili Soup had a Mexican-style flavor with meat, kidney beans, and plenty of vegetables. I enjoyed it so much that I brought beef soup and clam chowder. I was very satisfied with both soups. I spoke briefly with the owner and was impressed by his love for the soup and his kindness.
I can enjoy a variety of soups that are difficult to taste in Korea, and all four I tried were the best soups I've ever had, so I plan to try all the soups in the future. Although it is a difficult situation due to the coronavirus, I hope you continue to prosper and can visit often in the future.

This is an honest review of Salon de Muhe, a popular dessert restaurant in Hannam-dong. I ordered Isfahan Parfait (2.4) and Poire Belle Hélène (2.8). Although it is a bit pricey, I can understand it considering the quality. 🍨 Every single ingredient is luxurious and the plating is done with care. Coffee and orange juice also have a strong taste, so they are good to go with dessert. It's on the 3rd floor, so the view is great and the seats are comfortable, so I recommend it if you're looking for a good place to leisurely recharge!

reviews.author: byungho ahn (foodtrip81)
reviews.text: I went to Clubhouse Seoul, a unique cafe based on the concept of a clubhouse inside a golf course. It is located in a place with relatively few cars and people in Hannam-dong. There is a golf brand store on the first floor, a cafe on the second floor, and a rooftop on the third floor. When you come up to the cafe on the second floor, even if you don't know much about golf, you can tell that this cafe is themed around golf. Golf-related props are placed here and there, and combined with simple and sophisticated furniture, it has a small but cute feel. The drinks and desserts boast golf-related visuals, such as Buddy Latte, Bunker Shot Latte, and Hole-in-Nut. This cafe was created with the intention of someone who is serious about golf. The rooftop is also neatly decorated, so it's a place where you want to have chicken, pizza, and beer or wine during the season when it's good to spend time outside.
